h: Dad's Army, Flint Mines and a Revolutionary
p: Thetford has some cracking stories to go with its forest. The town will be forever linked with Dad's Army, as much of the classic sitcom was filmed in and around the area. There's a statue of Captain Mainwaring sitting on a bench by the river, and the Dad's Army Museum in the town is a nostalgic treat for fans of all ages.

Thetford was also the birthplace of Thomas Paine, the eighteenth-century writer whose ideas helped shape the American and French revolutions, and his statue stands in the town. Thetford Priory, the ruins of a large medieval priory looked after by English Heritage, is free to wander and full of atmosphere.

Out in the forest, Grime's Graves is a truly extraordinary site: a lunar-looking landscape of hollows that were once Neolithic flint mines. English Heritage looks after it, and it's a fascinating stop for anyone curious about how people lived thousands of years ago.

For the Go Ape course, plan on a couple of hours, and give yourselves breathing space before your briefing, as High Lodge can be busy at weekends and in the school holidays. Wear grippy footwear, bring water and pack a light jacket.

The Brecks have a drier climate than much of England, but the sandy soils can still be dusty or muddy, so keep a spare pair of socks and a bag for shoes in the car. Combined with the forest's trails and Thetford's history, it all adds up to a superb weekend.
